title: Smile House
statementMd:
A smile house is created to raise the mood. It has $*n*$ rooms. Some of the rooms are connected by doors. For each two rooms (number $*i*$ and $*j*$), which are connected by a door, Petya knows their value $*c*_{*ij*}$ — the value which is being added to his mood when he moves from room $*i*$ to room $*j*$.

Petya wondered whether he can raise his mood infinitely, moving along some cycle? And if he can, then what minimum number of rooms he will need to visit during one period of a cycle?

## Input

The first line contains two positive integers $*n*$ and $*m*$ (![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0d16348eee67d88f6667edf93a293fdb8b30603c.png)), where $*n*$ is the number of rooms, and $*m*$ is the number of doors in the Smile House. Then follows the description of the doors: $*m*$ lines each containing four integers $*i*$, $*j*$, $*c*_{*ij*}$ и $*c*_{*ji*}$ ($1 ≤ *i*, *j* ≤ *n*, *i* ≠ *j*,  - 10^{4} ≤ *c*_{*ij*}, *c*_{*ji*} ≤ 10^{4}$). It is guaranteed that no more than one door connects any two rooms. No door connects the room with itself.

## Output

Print the minimum number of rooms that one needs to visit during one traverse of the cycle that can raise mood infinitely. If such cycle does not exist, print number $0$.

## Note

Cycle is such a sequence of rooms $*a*_{1}$, $*a*_{2}$, ..., $*a*_{*k*}$, that $*a*_{1}$ is connected with $*a*_{2}$, $*a*_{2}$ is connected with $*a*_{3}$, ..., $*a*_{*k* - 1}$ is connected with $*a*_{*k*}$, $*a*_{*k*}$ is connected with $*a*_{1}$. Some elements of the sequence can coincide, that is, the cycle should not necessarily be simple. The number of rooms in the cycle is considered as $*k*$, the sequence's length. Note that the minimum possible length equals two.
statementZhMd:
<statement>
微笑之家用于提升心情。它有 $*n*$ 个房间，其中一些房间之间由门相连。对于由门相连的两个房间（编号为 $*i*$ 和 $*j*$），Petya 知道从房间 $*i*$ 移动到房间 $*j*$ 时会增加的心情值 $*c*_{*ij*}$。

Petya 想知道，他是否可以沿着某个环无限提升自己的心情？如果可以，那么在环的一次 traversing 过程中，他至少需要经过多少个房间？

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个正整数 $*n*$ 和 $*m*$ (![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0d16348eee67d88f6667edf93a293fdb8b30603c.png))，其中 $*n*$ 是房间的数量，$*m*$ 是微笑之家中门的数量。接下来是门的描述：接下来的 $*m*$ 行每行包含四个整数 $*i*$、$*j*$、$*c*_{*ij*}$ 和 $*c*_{*ji*}$（$1 ≤ *i*, *j* ≤ *n*$，$*i* ≠ *j*$，  - 10^{4} ≤ *c*_{*ij*}, *c*_{*ji*} ≤ 10^{4}$）。保证任意两个房间之间至多有一扇门。没有连接房间自身的门。

## 输出格式

输出能够无限提升心情的环，在一次遍历中需要经过的最少房间数。如果不存在这样的环，则输出 $0$。

## 说明

环是这样一个房间序列 $*a*_{1}$、$*a*_{2}$、...、$*a*_{*k*}$：$*a*_{1}$ 与 $*a*_{2}$ 相连，$*a*_{2}$ 与 $*a*_{3}$ 相连，...，$*a*_{*k* - 1}$ 与 $*a*_{*k*}$ 相连，$*a*_{*k*}$ 与 $*a*_{1}$ 相连。序列中的某些元素可以相同，也就是说，环不一定是简单环。环中房间的数量被定义为 $*k*$，即序列的长度。注意，可能的最小长度为二。
</statement>
